observations.title: Stratocumulus stratiformis undulatus
observations.description: An extensive, low-level layer of grey and whitish rounded cloud masses arranged in parallel, wave-like rolls across the sky. The undulating bands indicate gentle vertical wind shear at the base of a shallow temperature inversion.

observations.title: Nimbostratus praecipitatio
observations.description: A thick, featureless, dark grey cloud layer completely obscuring the sun and producing continuous, steady rain. Diffuse, ragged precipitation trails extend from the indistinct base toward the surface.

summaryReport.synopticHeadline: Morning transition from overcast, rain-producing Nimbostratus praecipitatio to broken low-level Stratus nebulosus over Thailand on 2026-09-24.
summaryReport.executiveSummary: Two observations recorded by Atlas Kaytser in Thailand on 2026-09-24 span a three-hour morning window from 06:30 to 09:40. Conditions began with an overcast (8/8) Nimbostratus praecipitatio layer producing continuous, steady rain, followed by a reduction in sky cover to 6/8 Stratus nebulosus by mid-morning.
summaryReport.weatherCorrelation: Surface weather parameters (temperature, humidity, wind, and barometric pressure) were unrecorded in both observations, preventing direct correlation with surface instrumentation. However, the 06:30 Nimbostratus praecipitatio record documents continuous, steady rain reaching the surface.
atmosphericSignals: Deep, moist, and stable-to-neutral stratiform ascent indicated by the overcast (8/8) Nimbostratus praecipitatio layer at 06:30.
Active precipitation processes evidenced by diffuse, ragged precipitation trails extending from the indistinct Nimbostratus base (600–2,000 m).
Post-precipitation boundary-layer saturation and low-level stability reflected in the 09:40 Stratus nebulosus (6/8) layer.
Gradual clearing or thinning of the thick frontal/synoptic cloud shield suggested by the decrease in total sky cover from 8/8 at 06:30 to 6/8 at 09:40.

taxonomicBreakdown.notes: Observed as Nimbostratus praecipitatio (Ns pra) at 06:30 with 8/8 oktas, base altitude 600–2,000 m, and continuous steady rain.
Observed as Stratus nebulosus (St neb) at 09:40 with 6/8 oktas; no field notes recorded.

notableTransitions.sequence: Overcast Nimbostratus praecipitatio (8/8) transitioning to broken Stratus nebulosus (6/8).
notableTransitions.meteorologicalMeaning: Indicates a shift from active, deep-layer stratiform precipitation to a shallower, non-precipitating low-level stratus deck as the primary rain-producing system weakened or moved away.

summaryReport.dataQualityNotes: Both observations were submitted by a single observer (Atlas Kaytser) in Thailand. Photo documentation is 50% (1 of 2 entries, present for Ns pra and absent for St neb). Surface weather readings are unrecorded for both entries, and the St neb entry lacks both altitude measurements and field notes.
